title: Unified Inference: Q2 2026 Roadmap, PRD, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Evelyn Chen
summary: This document consolidates the Q2 2026 product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference. It is intended for engineering, sales, and GTM stakeholders to align on scope, acceptance criteria, and launch plan.
overview: Purpose: Provide a single source of truth for the Unified Inference product increment for Q2 2026. Scope: API surface stability, Dedicated autoscaling improvements, Redwood Optimize v6 cost controls, pricing updates for per-token and reserved capacity, and a coordinated release across Hosted and Dedicated. Goals: 1) Reduce median token latency by 10% for standard generation workloads; 2) Improve Dedicated capacity autoscaling accuracy to 95% of target throughput under variable load; 3) Launch new pricing tiers and clear migration path for Reserved Capacity customers.
key_features_and_user_stories:
- Feature: Adaptive Autoscaling for Dedicated
  - User story: As a platform engineer, I want Dedicated pools to automatically provision burst nodes and scale down gracefully so my customers meet throughput SLAs without manual intervention.
- Feature: Bounded Quantization Profiles in Redwood Optimize v6
  - User story: As an ML engineer, I want suggested quantization profiles per-model and per-workload so I can reduce inference cost while respecting quality gates.
- Feature: Per-route Cost & Latency Controls
  - User story: As an SRE, I want per-route throttling and model routing policies to prioritize critical traffic and cap experimental feature costs.
- Feature: Pricing & Packaging update (Reserved Capacity v2)
  - User story: As a procurement lead, I want clearer tiers, burst add-ons, and migration credits to evaluate Dedicated contracts.
requirements:
Priority 1 (MUST):
1) Autoscaling controller: reach 95% accuracy (target throughput vs achieved) across synthetic and customer-derived load profiles.
2) API backward compatibility: existing text generation and chat endpoints must accept current client payloads without schema changes.
3) Billing alignment: per-token metering must capture quantized tokens and burst usage separately for invoicing.

Priority 2 (SHOULD):
1) Provide model-specific quantization recommendations with empirical cost/quality delta (ROUGE/BLEU/LLM-eval scores) for top 10 models.
2) Console: add per-route cost/latency controls UI and API.

Acceptance criteria (for each P1):
- Defined e2e test harness that replays production traffic (>= 72h) and verifies autoscaler metrics.
- No client-facing API changes in response schemas.
- Billing report includes: token_count, quantized_token_multiplier, burst_node_hours, reserved_commitment_id.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLO: median p50 token latency <= baseline * 0.9 for standard 1k-token gen.
- Availability: 99.95% for Hosted endpoints; 99.9% for Dedicated-managed control plane.
- Security: KMS integration for customer-managed keys (Private deployments) must be supported by GA in this increment.
design_spec:
High-level architecture:
- Components: API Gateway, Router, Serving Runtime (quantization-aware execution), Autoscaler, Billing Pipeline, Console.
- Autoscaler: controller that observes per-pool KPIs (queued reqs, tail latency, GPU utilization) and makes scaling decisions with a predictive model (time-series forecast + reactive thresholding).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
1) Predictive scaling vs reactive: we keep a hybrid approach — forecasts reduce cold-starts for predictable diurnal patterns; reactive triggers handle bursty traffic.
2) Prefix/KV cache interaction: autoscaler must be cache-aware to avoid thrashing; scaling down will prefer nodes with low cache residency.
3) Billing: instrumented on the ingress path to capture tokenization and downstream quantization multipliers; this avoids relying on runtime-side counters that vary by model.

Example autoscaler policy (YAML):
```
policy_name: hybrid-predictive-reactive
forecast_window: 15m
reactive_thresholds:
  queued_requests: 50
  gpu_utilization: 0.85
scale_up:
  step: 2
  cool_down: 60s
scale_down:
  step: 1
  cool_down: 5m
cache_awareness:
  avoid_evict_percent: 0.7
```

Ownership and interfaces:
- API Gateway: eng-platform (owner: Priya Desai)
- Autoscaler: eng-sre (owner: Marcus Li)
- Serving Runtime: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Ravi Kapoor)
- Billing Pipeline: finance-engineering (owner: Laura Martinez)

Open design questions:
- Exact predictive model features (time-of-day, customer cohort) to be finalized by ML infra team by 2026-05-30.
- Graceful cache transfer strategy when scaling down (checkpoint vs rebuild) — expected decision in design review 2026-05-27.
roadmap_and_themes:
Q2 2026 themes:
- Theme 1: Production economics (reduce cost per token while preserving quality)
- Theme 2: Predictable capacity (accurate autoscaling for Dedicated)
- Theme 3: Clear commercial motion (pricing clarity, migration credits, GTM enablement)

Milestones:
- 2026-05-10: Design review complete and approved
- 2026-05-20: Development kickoff (autoscaler + billing instrumentation)
- 2026-06-01: Internal dogfood across top 3 enterprise customers
- 2026-06-10: Beta release for Dedicated customers and GA for Redwood Optimize v6 features in Hosted
- 2026-06-24: Public pricing and docs update; sales enablement materials published

Dependencies:
- Billing pipeline schema changes (finance-and-legal) must be merged by 2026-05-25.
- Key management QA for Private deployments (security-and-compliance) must pass by 2026-06-02.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Autoscaler false positives causing over-provisioning. Mitigation: incremental rollout with 10% of traffic and kill-switch in console.
- Risk: Billing discrepancies during quantized runs. Mitigation: reconcile reports with a 7-day shadow mode and automated alerts to finance-engineering.
pricing_and_packaging_notes:
Summary of changes:
- Introduce Reserved Capacity v2 with three tiers: Standard, Performance, and Enterprise. Each tier includes baseline GPU-hours and a burst bucket billed at a discounted burst rate. Migration credits: up to 3 months of committed baseline for early renewals.
- Hosted API: small price reduction for high-volume embedding customers (>= 1B tokens/month) to better compete on price-sensitive workloads.

Pricing table (example):
- Hosted: API-gen: $0.0009 / token (standard), Embeddings: $0.0005 / unit for tier1
- Reserved v2 Standard: monthly commit $12k (includes 100 GPU-hrs), burst rate $3 / GPU-hr
- Reserved v2 Performance: monthly commit $48k (includes 450 GPU-hrs), burst rate $2 / GPU-hr
- Reserved v2 Enterprise: custom pricing, includes dedicated support and on-call SLAs

Billing mechanics and migration path:
1) New invoice fields: commitment_id, burst_usage_hours, effective_quantization_multiplier.
2) Migration credits calculated as: min(3 months, remaining term months) * baseline_monthly_commitment * 0.5 for eligible renewals.
3) Customers can enable shadow billing for 30 days to preview quantized cost impact.

GTM and enablement:
- Sales playbook: benefits checklist, migration worksheet, ROI calculator (spreadsheet) that compares current spend to Reserved v2 with suggested batching/quantization knobs.
- Marketing: publish example case studies showing 30% cost reduction for a SaaS customer after enabling Optimize v6 recommendations.
release_notes:
Release: Unified Inference v2026.06.10 (GA partial)
Release date: 2026-06-10
Components included:
- Autoscaler v2 (Dedicated) — Beta: Hybrid predictive/reactive scaling policy, initial rollout to 10% of Dedicated pools.
- Redwood Optimize v6 — GA for Hosted: Quantization profile suggestions and bounded profiles for top open models.
- Console: Per-route cost & latency controls UI (alpha) and API for programmatic route-level throttling.
- Billing: initial metering support for quantized tokens and burst_node_hours (shadow-mode enabled by default for first 7 days).

Notable fixes and improvements:
- Serving runtime: improved KV cache eviction to reduce tail-latency spikes (p95 down by ~12%).
- Router: fallback policy improvements to prefer lower-latency model variants during regional congestion.

Known issues:
1) Autoscaler may overshoot during synthetic traffic patterns with extreme spikes; mitigation: revert to reactive-only policy via admin flag.
2) Console UI: cost controls page may not display historical cost curves older than 14 days in Beta.

Post-release actions:
- 2026-06-11 to 2026-06-17: Monitor GA metrics: token latency, billing deltas, autoscale accuracy; daily status calls (eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, finance-engineering).
- 2026-06-20: Release notes published to public docs with migration FAQ.
- 2026-07-01: Complete rollout to 100% Dedicated pools contingent on autoscaler metrics meeting acceptance criteria.
rollout_and_metrics:
Rollout strategy:
1) Canary: internal only (inc. SRE and partner customers) for first 48 hours.
2) Beta: 10% Dedicated pools + opt-in enterprise customers for 2 weeks.
3) GA: 100% rollout after success criteria met (see metrics).

Success metrics (gates):
- Autoscaler accuracy: >= 95% target throughput for Beta customers over 72h test window.
- Latency: p50 token latency improvement >= 10% vs baseline on standard workloads.
- Billing reconciliation: discrepancies between shadow and final billing < 0.5% for first full billing cycle.

Signals & dashboards to monitor:
- eng-sre/autoscaler: scale_decisions/sec, avg_scale_latency, overshoot_count
- serving-runtime/latency: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tail cache miss rate
- finance-engineering/billing: shadow_billing_delta_percent, burst_hours_by_pool

Escalation path:
- Pager: eng-sre -> oncall runbook (see related page: confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/autoscaler-oncall)
- If billing discrepancies > 1% for 24h: emergency rollback to shadow-only and convene finance-engineering and product leads.
